Checked. N02 defines 'Tr^ss(Frob, V) = Σ_i Tr(Frob, (gr_i V)^{I_E})' with no convention, N06 and N14 write Tr^ss(Frob_y, …), and KP18 p. 212 gives none either. Pappas–Zhu arXiv:1110.5588v4 (SHA-256 cbb87912…, the extraction's copy) §9.d.1 fixes 'σ is the geometric Frobenius element', and route 10's brief asks for the geometric Frobenius. The GL_2 check re-derived: at Iwahori (Γ_0(p)) level with μ = (1, 0), Adm(μ) = {τ, τs_1, τs_0}, and q^{1/2}z_μ = T_{τs_1} + T_{τs_0} + (1 − q)T_τ. At a crossing point of the semistable special fibre R^0Ψ = Q̄_ℓ and R^1Ψ = Q̄_ℓ(−1) with trivial inertia on each, so Tr^ss = 1 − q for the geometric Frobenius and 1 − q^{−1} for the arithmetic one. (4.7.12) therefore holds only for the geometric Frobenius; at smooth points and at hyperspecial level both give 1. Medium is right: as extracted, N14 is false under one of the two readings its items allow. The fix is right. For the fixer: Pappas–Zhu §9.d.3 prints A_μ with q^{+(ρ,μ)}, while the geometric convention needs q^{−(ρ,μ)}, which is what KP18 p. 215 uses.

Checked. S14 has prerequisites S10, S12 and S13 only, and no item states that prime-to-p level change on the Hodge models is finite étale (P12, S22, A03 and finite-level-quotient-etale-local-structure do not). The proof of Proposition 4.3.7 (pp. 190–191) uses it with Proposition 4.2.2: 'by what we have shown above together with Proposition 4.2.2, the maps S_{K'°} → S_{K'} → S_K are finite étale. Since the composite of these maps factors through S_{K°}, it follows that S_{K°} → S_K is finite étale.' Proposition 4.2.2 is one of the results E3 says need a very good embedding, and KPZ26's corrected Proposition 7.1.11(1) (linked from S14) assumes it. The replacement argument, that normalization commutes with finite étale change of prime-to-p level, exists only in E3's review reason. The remark on étale surjectivity is right: from g∘f étale one gets g étale only over the image of f and with f flat, so the step silently uses that S_{K'°} → S_{K°} is étale and surjective. That holds (for instance as a free quotient when K'^p is normal and small), so it is an omitted step, not an error. Medium is right.
Adjustments to the fix: state the new item as 'for K'^p ⊂ K^p (sufficiently small), 𝒮^-_{K'} → 𝒮^-_K, 𝒮_{K'} → 𝒮_K and 𝒮_{K'°} → 𝒮_{K°} are finite étale and surjective', proved from Siegel level base change and normalization commuting with étale base change, and make it missing on route 9 with S14. Also add S14's small-level torsor step (the first half of the proposition) to its prerequisites, and say in S14's note that KPZ26 Prop. 7.1.11(1) is proved under the very good assumption, so this item is what lets 4.3.7 stand without it.

Checked on pp. 145–146.
- (a) The proof of Lemma 1.4.6 asserts 'Therefore, H^1(𝒦, G) = {1}' from cd(𝒦) = 2. For finite k of odd characteristic that step is false. Take the split G_2 and ε ∈ W^× lifting a non-square of k: the Pfister form ⟨⟨ε, u, p⟩⟩ is anisotropic over the completion of 𝒦 = Frac(W[[u]]) at (p), by Springer's theorem twice (residue field k((u)), then k), so it is the norm form of an octonion division algebra and H^1(𝒦, G_2) ≠ 1. Whether the lemma's conclusion fails for finite k is not settled by this, as the finding says.
- (b) Hu, Algebra Number Theory 7 (2013), Theorem 4.5 (Artin–Gabber) gives cd_ℓ = 3 for ℓ different from the residue characteristic only; it says nothing about cd_p, and only cd(𝒦) ≥ 3 is needed.
- (c) The proof of Proposition 1.4.3 begins 'We begin by considering the case when k is algebraically closed' (p. 145); that is what makes the tame splitting field cyclic in Step 2, and for finite k the extension K_0(√ε, √p)/K_0 is tame with group (Z/2)².
Low is right. One addition to the fix: E17's own reason and review also say 'cd_ℓ = cd_p = 3', and should say 'cd_ℓ(𝒦) = 3 for ℓ ≠ p (Hu 2013, Thm. 4.5)'.
